assessment.nobel_worthiness: KPZ is a prime example of a simple stochastic model whose scaling exponents and fluctuation statistics are universal across growth, interfaces, directed polymers, and quantum and driven systems. It links non-equilibrium statistical mechanics to random-matrix (Tracy-Widom) statistics, which is a direct bridge to my own field. The idea is clean, mechanistic and analysable, and its reach is very wide.
assessment.attribution: The 1986 equation is due to Kardar, Parisi and Zhang. Parisi is not in the credited names (he already holds a prize for other work), so a fair configuration rests on Kardar and Zhang for theory and Takeuchi for the decisive liquid-crystal experimental confirmation of the universal distributions. Exact solutions (Johansson, Sasamoto-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel and others) are not credited, which leaves part of the credit unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation of KPZ-class scaling is solid and independent (turbulent liquid crystals, and later optical and cold-atom systems). Recognition is timely, since the universality picture has stabilised and the field is still productive.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would treat the mathematical exact solutions as essential and so complicate a three-person split.
Absence of Parisi from the credited names may affect how the discovery is framed.
I am working from memory of the literature and have not verified details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock (magic-wavelength trapping) gives fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and is changing time metrology, geodesy and fundamental-constant tests. The core idea is simple, general and elegant, and it has had a large and lasting effect on precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first clock. Ye developed the highest-performance Sr clocks and the many-body and comb-linked advances. The credited pair fits a two-person prize. Others (Ludlow, Kimble, Takamoto and more) have contributed, and the credit boundary with frequency-comb work, which was already recognised in 2005, is a point of discussion.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. There are many independent clocks at 1e-18 or better, and the SI redefinition of the second is under discussion, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 comb prize and with the 2012 ion-trap prize may lower the novelty argument for some members.
Allocation relative to other strontium and ytterbium clock groups is not fully clear from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models with controlled parameters, so strongly correlated matter becomes tunable. The Mott insulator transition, single-site microscopy and quantum gas simulation have already influenced condensed-matter physics and statistical mechanics. It is physics that is both understood and controlled.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and others) supplied the proposal and theory, Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott-insulator experiment and quantum gas microscopy. Jaksch, Hänsch, Esslinger and Ketterle's group have claims as well, so a three-person set leaves some claims unresolved. The credited trio is workable.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation worldwide. Quantum simulation is established, although whether it surpasses classical computation for useful problems is still being decided. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Cirac-Zoller candidate on the theory side.
Credit among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, Hänsch and Jaksch is not cleanly separable.
Uncertain how far the committee sees the field as past the 2001 BEC prize and the 2012 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators introduced a new organising principle (topology and symmetry protection) for electronic phases. Kane and Mele gave the clean theoretical model and Z2 classification, and Molenkamp's HgTe experiments showed the edge transport. The scientific effect has been very large, and it extends to photonics and cold atoms.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are central on theory. Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, who proposed HgTe, and Fu-Kane (3D) are not credited, so the allocation among theory is not complete. Molenkamp is the natural experimentalist. The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions, which makes the proposed set a plausible follow-on.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many independent experiments (ARPES on 3D TIs, quantum anomalous Hall). Material applications are still developing, but the physics is mature.
uncertainties: Missing credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and for 3D topological insulators (Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents).
Some members may feel the 2016 prize already acknowledged the topological theme.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture gives a unified, minimal description of the onset of rigidity in disordered matter, with critical scaling, isostaticity and soft modes. It suits the statistical-mechanics view of a mechanism that explains a very wide set of systems (foams, grains, emulsions, glasses). It is cleaner and more general than many applied descriptions.
assessment.attribution: The 1998 Liu-Nagel proposal and the 2003 O'Hern-Silbert-Liu-Nagel work form a natural two-person credit. Others, such as O'Hern, Silbert, Wyart, Torquato and Behringer, contributed key results. The pair is supported by the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, with simulations and some experiments in agreement. The exact nature of the transition (critical point or not, links to glass physics) is still debated, so the interpretation is not entirely stable.
uncertainties: Open questions about the relationship with the glass transition and about upper-critical dimension.
Experimental tests of criticality in real systems are harder than in simulations.
Credit for the isostatic and marginal-stability analysis is shared with others who are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory showed that a polar ordered phase with long-range order exists in two dimensions in a non-equilibrium system, in conflict with the Mermin-Wagner theorem, and gave anomalous scaling. This is a conceptual advance of the kind I value: a simple model, a rigorous theory and a universal mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek proposed the minimal model (1995), and Toner and Tu produced the continuum theory (1995, 1998) with the renormalisation-group analysis. Others (Chaté, Marchetti, Ramaswamy, Cavagna and Giardina) also contributed, particularly on first-order transitions and experimental tests. The three credited names give a reasonable set.
assessment.maturity: Quantitative experimental confirmation of the exponents in real flocks or active colloids is less clear than for KPZ, and the nature of the transition has been revised (discontinuous in the Vicsek model). The field is therefore less mature.
uncertainties: Weak direct experimental verification of the predicted exponents.
Debate on the order of the flocking transition.
Whether the committee regards active matter as ready for recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mapping the acoustic peaks of the CMB turned cosmology into a precision science (geometry, baryon density, dark matter, dark energy). The physics of the acoustic oscillations is a well-understood mechanism that provides robust parameter constraints. The impact is lasting and basic.
assessment.attribution: Credit is diffuse: Sunyaev and Zeldovich (and Peebles and Yu) for the acoustic physics, WMAP and Planck teams for the measurement, and earlier balloon experiments (BOOMERanG, MAXIMA). A prize for Mather and Smoot (2006) and for Peebles (2019) already recognised parts of the field, which makes the allocation hard. My choice of Bennett, Spergel and Sunyaev is a judgement and others could fairly make a different choice.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by WMAP, Planck, ACT and SPT in agreement. Timely and mature, although recognition of the field has partly been given already.
uncertainties: Large collaboration structure and diffuse credit.
Overlap with 2006 and 2019 prizes.
Whether Page or Puget should displace one of my picks.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and the entanglement-based protocol of Ekert established the idea of information-theoretic secure key distribution, and the teleportation protocol was a founding result of quantum information. The ideas are simple and deep, and they link physics to computation and communication.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are clearly central (BB84 and teleportation). Ekert's 1991 protocol is the key independent contribution. The three credited names fit a prize well, although teleportation also involved Crépeau, Jozsa, Peres and Wootters, who are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with commercial and satellite demonstrations. The 2022 prize on entanglement experiments recognised related foundations, so some members may see the area as partly covered. Practical security is still affected by implementation issues.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize.
The B014 and B059 entries look like the same discovery, and I only rank one of them.
Unsettled credit for the teleportation protocol.
